events.title: Produce Pop-Up
events.description: Produce Pop-Up is a twice-weekly organic farmstand open to all members of the UC Santa Cruz community. The program is dedicated to increasing access to fresh, healthy, and affordable organic produce, with offerings sourced from the UCSC Farm and other local organic growers.

events.title: Building Better Food Policy Councils with Nessa Richman
events.description: Join us in the Oakes College Mural Room for a book talk by Nessa Richman followed by a panel conversation with campus and community food systems professionals exploring civic engagement and how we can foster a more just and sustainable food system for all.

events.title: Scotts Valley Farmers' Market
events.description: Seasonal farmers' market with local produce, prepared foods and live music.
events.recurrence: Saturdays, 8:00 AM to noon, May 2 to November 21

events.title: Westside Farmers' Market
events.description: A year-round market with regional produce, prepared foods, Market Match and seasonal special events.

events.title: Open Farm Tours: South County Farms
events.description: Self-guided visits to Blossom's Biodynamic Farm, Esperanza Community Farms, Dos Aguilas Olive Grove, Live Earth Farm, Thomas Farm, Live Oak School Farm and Birdsong Orchard Farm. The $25 Friends & Family Pass covers up to five people per car for both tour days.

events.title: Live Earth Farm U-pick, Strawberries Open
events.description: The farm currently lists strawberries as OPEN at $3/lb. Other crops open as they ripen. No reservation is needed; field abundance can change, so check the official crop-status page before leaving. No dogs.
events.recurrence: Saturdays and Sundays, 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM, through late October; field abundance permitting

events.title: Live Oak Farmers' Market
events.description: A year-round neighborhood market with regional produce, meals and a seasonal music series.

events.title: Open Farm Tours: North County Farms
events.description: Self-guided visits to Beeline Blooms, Post Street Farm, Flip Flop Farm, Rodoni Farms, Pie Ranch, Homeless Garden Project, Santa Cruz Permaculture and Swanton Berry Farm. The $25 Friends & Family Pass covers up to five people per car for both tour days.

events.title: A Presentation by Rick Flores: The Uses of Native Plants
events.description: Attend the CNPS chapter meeting on October 12 to hear UCSC Arboretum and Botanic Garden Director Rick Flores explore seasonal harvest, nuts, berries, and edible greens.

events.title: UCSC Arboretum Volunteer Information Session
events.description: Learn about volunteering in the gardens, greenhouses, gift shop and retail nursery during a roughly 45-minute orientation and easy garden walk. Submit the volunteer interest form before attending.
events.recurrence: Second Tuesday of each month, 10:00 to 11:00 AM

events.title: Sustainability & Dining at UCSC
events.description: Join UCSC Dining and campus sustainability partners for a one-hour lunchtime webinar on how food, dining operations, and campus food systems connect to sustainability, basic needs, and climate action.

events.title: Felton Farmers' Market
events.description: Seasonal farmers' market with regional produce, prepared foods and live music.
events.recurrence: Tuesdays, 1:30 to 5:30 PM, May 5 to October 27

events.title: Downtown Santa Cruz Farmers' Market
events.description: Regional organic produce, pasture-raised meats, eggs, dairy, seafood and artisan goods.

events.title: Kids Garden Club at Beach Flats Garden
events.description: A free weekly club where children from the Homework Club at the Beach Flats Community Center tend their own zone of the garden. Runs with the Community Bridges youth program school year. Volunteers are welcome and complete an onboarding with Community Bridges. Club de los jardineritos, cada miercoles.
events.organizer: City of Santa Cruz Parks & Recreation

events.title: English Club in the Garden at Beach Flats
events.description: An informal free club supporting Spanish-speaking community members who want to practice and improve their English, held in the garden rather than a classroom. Volunteers welcome. Club de ingles en el jardin, cada miercoles.
events.organizer: City of Santa Cruz Parks & Recreation

events.title: Boulder Creek Farmers Market
events.description: Shop local farms, artisan goods and street-food vendors with live music. Dogs are not allowed in the park during market hours under county health rules. Check the organizer's weekly updates for the current vendor and food-truck lineup.
events.organizer: Farm Success Partners & Boulder Creek Recreation and Park District

events.title: 2026 Harvest Festival
events.description: Connect with community on the campus farm at the annual Harvest Festival! Harvest Fest will have activities for all ages including face painting, flower pressing, pumpkin painting, cider pressing, tractor rides, live music from Sambada and Lucas Lawson, and more!

events.title: North Stars of Emancipation: Navigating Movements and Institutions to Change Food Systems
events.description: Dr. Antonio Roman-Alcal has been participating in food and farming movements in California for over two decades. He's founded urban farms, taught organic horticulture, and made documentary films about why food systems continue to be unsustainable.

events.venue: School food programs and gardens across Santa Cruz County
events.description: A professional tour for garden educators, nutrition educators and school food-service staff, featuring resilient school gardens and scratch-cooking meal programs. Cost: $200; financial assistance and educator discounts are available.

events.title: Advanced Tractor Skills Workshop
events.description: Are you a farmer with 2 to 4 years of tractor operating experience ready to move beyond basic driving and machine operation? Join our 2-day Advanced Tractor Skills Workshop focusing on developing greater confidence, precision, efficiency, and control in real field conditions.

events.description: Bring extra seedlings, cuttings, produce, seeds or garden supplies to share. No contribution is required.

events.description: Learn to make a beautiful and long-lasting dried floral and succulent pumpkin that can be used as a stunning centerpiece in this "make and take" workshop, just in time for the holidays.

events.title: Plant Keying with Lucy, 4th Monday each month
events.description: 5:30 to 7:30pm at the Horticulture 2 Meeting Hall Join Lucy Ferneyhough, our Associate Director and Native Plant Program Project Manager, who will be hosting keying sessions on the fourth Monday of every month.
